name: Zinc
short: Common-cold trials: zinc as treatment probably raised non-serious adverse events. Case reports link zinc supplements and zinc overload to copper deficiency, causing anaemia or nerve damage.
text: In a 2024 Cochrane review of zinc for preventing and treating the common cold (34 studies in adults and children), non-serious adverse events were probably more common when zinc was used to treat colds (moderate-certainty evidence; 16 studies, 2,084 participants), and no treatment study provided information on serious adverse events; when zinc was used to prevent colds, it is uncertain whether it changes the risk of adverse events or increases the risk of serious adverse events (very low- and low-certainty evidence). A case report describes severe anaemia from copper deficiency caused by zinc supplement use; a review of 55 published cases of copper deficiency myelopathy (spinal cord damage) listed zinc overload among the risk factors, and neurological recovery after copper treatment was only partial. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
